title: Nonarchimedean finite-evaluation bounds and parameter calculus
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and use $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and its absolute value from [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let $X,Y$ be nonempty compact topological spaces, $I$ a finite set, $b_j:Y\to X$ continuous for $j\in I$, and $\lambda_j\in\mathbf Q_\ell$. Fix a real number $B\geq0$ such that $|\lambda_j|_\ell\leq B$ for all $j$. For every normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space $V$ satisfying $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$ and $\|av\|=|a|_\ell\|v\|$, with its norm topology and with no completeness assumption, the formula
$$L_V:C(X,V)\to C(Y,V),\qquad (L_Vf)(y)=\sum_{j\in I}\lambda_j f(b_j(y))$$
defines a linear map, has finite supremum norms, and satisfies $\|L_Vf\|_\infty\leq B\|f\|_\infty$. Every linear coefficient subspace $W\subseteq V$, whether or not closed, is preserved: $f(X)\subseteq W$ implies $(L_Vf)(Y)\subseteq W$. For any topological parameter space $S$ and continuous $f:S\times X\to V$, the formula
$$(L_{V,S}f)(s,y)=\sum_{j\in I}\lambda_j f(s,b_j(y))$$
is continuous on $S\times Y$, and its restriction to each $s$ is $L_V(f(s,-))$. Any pointwise linear identities between such evaluation operators therefore hold on parameter families when they hold on every slice. Empty finite lists give zero operators, and an empty parameter space gives the unique family.
The class of fixed finite evaluation formulas is closed under composition with each other and under precomposition by fixed continuous maps, independently of $V$: if $Z$ is nonempty compact, $c_k:Z\to Y$ is continuous and $(Mf)(z)=\sum_k\mu_k f(c_k(z))$, then
$$(M L_Vf)(z)=\sum_{k,j}\mu_k\lambda_j f(b_j(c_k(z))).$$
In particular, for a positive integer $m$ prime to $\ell$, every coefficient $k/m$ with $k\in\mathbf Z$ has $|k/m|_\ell\leq1$. Thus a formula whose coefficients are integers divided by $m$, including after precomposition by continuous coordinate changes, has norm bound one, preserves all linear coefficient subspaces, and gives continuous parameter families. These conclusions include $V=0$ and cochain domains consisting of a single point.

proof.text: Fixed scalar multiplication is Lipschitz: $\|a v-a w\|=|a|_\ell\|v-w\|$. Addition is continuous since $\|(v+w)-(v_0+w_0)\|\leq\max(\|v-v_0\|,\|w-w_0\|)$. Thus each $y\mapsto\lambda_j f(b_j(y))$ is continuous, and induction on the finite list gives continuity of $L_Vf$, starting with the constant zero map. Distributivity in $V$ gives $L_V(f+g)=L_Vf+L_Vg$ and $L_V(af)=aL_Vf$ pointwise, hence the asserted linear map.

proof.text: Use Mathlib's ContinuousMap.norm_coe_le_norm to bound each pointwise norm by the continuous-map norm, giving BddAbove for both ranges. ContinuousMap.norm_eq_iSup_norm identifies both norms with their real indexed suprema. These lemmas apply on compact spaces without separation or completeness assumptions, so a separate extreme-value proof is unnecessary.

proof.text: The assumed ultrametric inequality gives IsUltrametricDist V by isUltrametricDist_of_forall_norm_add_le_max_norm. For each summand, norm_smul and mul_le_mul bound its norm by B times the continuous-map norm of f. IsUltrametricDist.norm_sum_le_of_forall_le_of_nonneg bounds the finite sum, including an empty index type. ContinuousMap.norm_le turns these pointwise bounds into the asserted norm estimate. A submodule contains each scalar multiple and their finite sum, so it is preserved without closedness.

proof.text: For a parameter space $S$, the map $(s,y)\mapsto(s,b_j(y))$ is continuous: the inverse image of a basic product open $U\times O$ is $U\times b_j^{-1}(O)$. Composing with the given continuous $f$ and using the continuous fixed scalar multiplication and finite addition of step 1 proves continuity of $L_{V,S}f$. Substitution of a fixed $s$ gives exactly $L_V(f(s,-))$. An asserted pointwise identity holds at $(s,y)$ by its slice identity at $s$; equality of functions is pointwise equality. Empty $S$ has the unique function to $V$.

proof.text: Expand the composite at $z$: $\sum_k\mu_k\sum_j\lambda_j f(b_j(c_k(z)))=\sum_k\sum_j(\mu_k\lambda_j)f((b_j\circ c_k)(z))$, by finite distributivity. The index set of pairs is finite and each $b_j\circ c_k$ is continuous, giving the claimed finite formula. Precomposition by a fixed continuous map $u$ simply replaces $b_j$ by $b_j\circ u$. These formulas and their coefficients involve only the original maps and scalars, independently of $V$. With either list empty the same expansion is the zero sum.

proof.text: Padic.norm_natCast_eq_one_iff gives norm one for m from coprimality, and Padic.norm_int_le_one bounds every integer. By norm_div, every integer divided by m has norm at most one. Apply the already proved finite-evaluation bound with B = 1 both to the original coordinate maps and to their precompositions. The argument includes zero coefficients, empty finite index types, zero vector spaces and singleton compact domains.
